segments: 559. The Eleventh Jubilee. {OCR?}
The Hunnish (Mongol) Kings.
Out of fear of them, they suffered a great loss.
And they brought their loads inside the city,
and placed them in the cloth-merchants' market,
because all the provisions of the citizens were there;
they thought that they would by no means neglect the guarding of such a place.
Therefore, they were jostling and pressing against one another
to bring in their property.
The citizens as well were carrying and bringing there from their houses gold, silver, fabrics, and clothing of various kinds.
And so, after they were assembled,
the raiders came and easily broke down the gates of the market,
and entered and took everything they found there.
For many youths of the citizens were standing at the gate of the market,
and whenever the raiders came out carrying plunder,
they would snatch it from them and flee.
And others, their horses
which they were leaving at the gate of the market,
they would take and flee.
And thus all that day,
from morning until evening,
they roamed through the streets of the city,
and carried off horses, mules, donkeys, and oxen without number.
And they bound male and female slaves,
about five hundred souls,
most of them being Arabs (Muslims) and Jews.
The Christians, however, were very few,
only those who were found from the courtyard of the Naqib.
Indeed, one faithful man, a remarkable goldsmith, was killed;
for he wanted to rescue his young son from their hands,
so they struck him with a sword,
and after three days he died.
Of the accursed ones, however, about ten souls perished,
because while they were roaming about in the city
and entering streets that had no exits,
they were stoning them with stones and killing them.
And if the Arab (Muslim) citizens had known
that the raiders of their own faith would thus mercilessly abuse {OCR?} them and take them captive,
they would have killed most of them in the narrow streets of the city,
and in the beginning, again, they would not have been able to enter it so easily.
And when they were deceived,
behold, they were biting their fingers without any profit.
The raiders, however, all that day
brought out the captives outside the city,
and remained there when it grew dark.
